q: Vector P has rectangular components Px and Py. The magnitude of vector P is:
x: The two rectangular components are at right angles, so by Pythagoras the magnitude is √(Px² + Py²). Simply adding the components ignores the right angle between them.

q: A particle is pulled by a 12 N force due east and a 5 N force due north. How large is the net pull on it?
x: The forces are perpendicular, so R = √(12² + 5²) = √169 = 13 N. 17 N would be correct only if the forces acted in the same direction.

q: A vector of magnitude 10 N points 30° below the positive x-axis. Its x- and y-components are (cos 30° = √3/2, sin 30° = 0.5):
x: x = 10 cos 30° = 5√3 N, and y = −10 sin 30° = −5 N because the vector points below the x-axis. Swapping sin and cos gives the wrong pair.

q: Adding the vectors 3î + 4ĵ and î − 4ĵ gives a resultant of:
x: Adding components: x = 3 + 1 = 4 and y = 4 − 4 = 0. The resultant is 4î, i.e. 4 units along the positive x-axis.

q: Two forces of 10 N each act on a body, one along the positive x-axis and the other at 60° to it. Using rectangular components (cos 60° = 0.5, sin 60° = √3/2), the magnitude of the resultant is:
x: Rx = 10 + 10 cos 60° = 15 N and Ry = 10 sin 60° = 5√3 N. R = √(225 + 75) = √300 = 10√3 N. 20 N would need the forces to be parallel.

q: A vector of magnitude 10 units has an x-component of 6 units. The magnitude of its y-component is:
x: Magnitude² = x² + y², so y² = 100 − 36 = 64 and y = 8 units. Subtracting 10 − 6 = 4 ignores the right angle between components.

q: A vector has an x-component of −8 units and a y-component of +6 units. Its magnitude and the quadrant in which it lies are:
x: Magnitude = √(64 + 36) = 10 units. A negative x-component with a positive y-component places the vector in the second quadrant.

q: Two vectors of magnitudes P and Q point in the same direction. Their scalar product is:
x: P · Q = PQ cos θ, and θ = 0° for vectors in the same direction, so cos θ = 1 and the scalar product is PQ.

q: The scalar product of a vector P with itself, P · P, is equal to:
o: The square of the magnitude of P
x: The angle between a vector and itself is 0°, so P · P = P × P × cos 0° = P². It is a scalar, not a vector.

q: Vector P = 3î − 2ĵ + k̂ and vector Q = 2î + 4ĵ + 2k̂. The angle between P and Q is:
x: P · Q = (3)(2) + (−2)(4) + (1)(2) = 6 − 8 + 2 = 0. A zero scalar product of non-zero vectors means they are perpendicular.

q: A force F = (4î + 3ĵ) N moves a body through a displacement d = (5î) m. The work done by the force is:
x: W = F · d = (4)(5) + (3)(0) = 20 J. Only the component of force along the displacement does work; 25 J wrongly uses the full 5 N magnitude.

q: Power delivered by a force can be written as the scalar product of:
x: P = F · v, a scalar product. Force · displacement gives work, not power.

q: Two vectors of magnitudes 4 units and 3 units have a scalar product of −6. The angle between them is (cos 120° = −0.5):
x: cos θ = (−6)/(4 × 3) = −0.5, so θ = 120°. A negative scalar product means the angle is more than 90°.

q: Vector P = 2î + aĵ and vector Q = 3î − 2ĵ are perpendicular to each other. The value of a is:
x: Perpendicular vectors have P · Q = 0: 2 × 3 + a × (−2) = 0, so 6 − 2a = 0 and a = 3.

q: Two vectors P and Q are inclined at an angle θ. The magnitude of their vector product is:
x: |P × Q| = PQ sin θ. PQ cos θ is the scalar product.

q: Using the cyclic rule for unit vectors, the cross product of k̂ with î (k̂ × î) gives:
x: Following the cyclic order î → ĵ → k̂ → î: î × ĵ = k̂, ĵ × k̂ = î and k̂ × î = ĵ. Reversing the order would give −ĵ.

q: The vector product of a vector P with itself, P × P, is:
x: The angle between P and itself is 0° and sin 0° = 0, so P × P is the null vector. P² is the scalar product P · P.

q: Two vectors keep their magnitudes but the angle between them is varied. Their cross product has its largest magnitude at an angle of:
x: |P × Q| = PQ sin θ, and sin θ has its largest value of 1 at θ = 90°. At 0° and 180° it is zero.

q: The adjacent sides of a parallelogram are 5 cm and 4 cm long with an angle of 30° between them (sin 30° = 0.5). Using the vector product, the area of the parallelogram is:
x: Area = |P × Q| = PQ sin θ = 5 × 4 × 0.5 = 10 cm². 20 cm² forgets the sin θ factor.

q: Which of the following physical quantities is defined as a vector product of two vectors?
x: Torque τ = r × F is a vector product. Work and power are scalar products, and kinetic energy is not a product of two vectors.

q: Work out the cross product (î + ĵ) × (î − ĵ):
x: For vectors in the xy-plane, the cross product is (PxQy − PyQx)k̂ = (1 × (−1) − 1 × 1)k̂ = −2k̂.
